gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much each case adds to an iPhone 17 Pro's 206 g. SUPCASE's UB Pro adds 147.8 g, about 72% more weight (147.8 / 206). Spigen's Tough Armor T adds about 51 g, about 25% more (1.8 oz ≈ 51 g / 206 g). SUPCASE's MagSafe UB Grip Pro adds 80 g, about 39% more (80 / 206), and still carries a 20 ft drop claim.
standout_why: I could not open either cited rival. travelandleisure.com and goodhousekeeping.com were both blocked to WebFetch, and curl was not allowed, so I can't rule out that either one lists case weights. I did read two top results. The rottenwifi.com 'Best Protective Phone Cases of 2026' page gives drop-height claims (UAG 25 ft, Pelican 21 ft, Speck 13 ft) but no case weight or thickness for any case. The Ezvid Wiki 'Best Rugged Phone Cases' page (the cloudfront.net URL) gives prices and maker drop claims, also with no weights, and says outright that no independent lab tested the cases. Neither page compares a case's weight to the phone's weight or works out cost per foot of rated drop height.
decides: It supports ChatGPT's split between maximum protection and protection without bulk, and puts a number on that bulk. The SUPCASE UB Pro, ChatGPT's 'budget heavy-duty' pick, nearly doubles the phone's weight (about 354 g together). Its iPhone 17 Pro page also says it does NOT support MagSafe, which ChatGPT did not mention. A shopper who wants SUPCASE-level drop claims with MagSafe and less weight should look at the UB Grip Pro: 80 g, a 20 ft claim and $43.99 on SUPCASE's store. On cost, UAG's own store has the Monarch Pro for iPhone 17 Pro at $42.95 today, not the $79.95 ChatGPT showed. That makes it the cheapest per rated foot of the cases with a stated height ($42.95 / 25 ft = $1.72/ft). I could not source the Defender Pro's weight from OtterBox, so this does not yet rank ChatGPT's top pick on weight.
